screening_decisions.reason: Prospective RCT in frozen shoulder (42 patients) randomly allocated to steroid, mobilisations, ice, or no treatment. All taught pendular exercises. Includes manual therapy (mobilisation) and exercise comparisons relevant to the review.
Observational incidence study in general practice, not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial. No intervention comparison for efficacy.
Review of textbook principles of joint mobilization. Not a primary clinical trial.

Open RCT comparing physical therapies (exercises, TENS, IRR) alone versus the same physical therapies plus arthrographic distension and intra-articular steroid. Because both groups received exercise-based physical therapy, the comparison does not address the efficacy of manual therapy or exercise versus placebo/no intervention/different manual therapy or exercise; it addresses an invasive adjunct (distension). Does not fit the review's primary comparisons of interest.
Methodological study comparing trial protocols/registry entries with published reports. Not a trial of adhesive capsulitis treatment.

Explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial investigating deep transverse friction massage (manual therapy) and capsular stretching (exercise) in idiopathic adhesive capsulitis. Abstract is minimal, but stated design and topic meet inclusion criteria.

RCT randomly allocating frozen shoulder patients to two different exercise programs (glenohumeral ROM exercises vs glenohumeral plus scapulothoracic exercises). Directly compares exercise interventions relevant to the review.

Randomized multiple-treatment trial comparing three mobilization techniques (end-range, mid-range, and mobilization with movement) in subjects with frozen shoulder syndrome. Compares different manual therapy approaches.

Study comparing Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) movement patterns versus conventional free exercises in chronic peri-arthritis (frozen shoulder). Population and interventions (exercise approaches) are relevant. Abstract does not explicitly state randomization, so design will need confirmation at full-text review.
Pilot study randomizing patients with primary adhesive capsulitis to antero-posterior versus postero-anterior glide mobilization. RCT comparing two manual therapy techniques.
Two-stage cross-sectional population survey estimating prevalence of upper limb disorders. Not a treatment trial.
Multiple-subject case report (n=7) describing end-range mobilization. Not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial.

Placebo-controlled RCT (93 subjects) with adhesive capsulitis randomized to intra-articular corticosteroid plus supervised physiotherapy, corticosteroid alone, saline plus physiotherapy, or saline alone. All taught home exercise. Includes relevant comparisons of supervised physiotherapy/exercise versus control.

RCT (156 participants) with adhesive capsulitis, randomized after joint distension to manual therapy and directed exercise versus placebo (sham ultrasound). Compares a combination of manual therapy and exercise against a placebo control in the target population.
Observational measurement study evaluating the responsiveness of the Shoulder Disability Questionnaire. Not a treatment trial.

Non-randomized comparative study (75 patients allocated to physical therapy, acupuncture, or both). No mention of randomization or quasi-randomization; unequal group sizes suggest convenience allocation.
Systematic review and cost-effectiveness analysis of frozen shoulder management. Not a primary study.

Study comparing anterior versus posterior glide mobilisation in adhesive capsulitis, but abstract does not indicate randomised or quasi-randomised design. Without evidence of eligible study design, it is excluded.
Methodological study examining outcome reporting bias across Cochrane reviews. Not a trial of adhesive capsulitis treatment.

Title mentions frozen shoulder, but abstract describes an inception cohort study of patients recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. Mismatch means this record does not describe an eligible frozen shoulder RCT.

Randomized clinical trial (87 patients) with frozen shoulder comparing corticosteroid injection, physiotherapy, and combination therapy. Includes relevant comparisons of physiotherapy versus other interventions.

RCT (40 patients) randomised to Cyriax rehabilitation (deep friction massage and mobilisation exercises) versus conventional physical therapy (modalities plus stretching and home exercise) in adhesive capsulitis. Compares manual therapy plus exercise versus conventional rehabilitation.
Prospective observational study of the natural history of frozen shoulder (49 patients followed for 5-10 years). No randomised intervention comparison.
Methodological paper proposing heterogeneity measures for meta-analysis. Not a clinical trial.
Methodological chapter on reporting biases. Not a primary study.
Prospective observational study of 40 frozen shoulder patients followed for 40-48 months. No randomised intervention comparison.
RCT (20 patients) randomly assigned to passive joint mobilization plus active exercises versus active exercises alone in adhesive capsulitis. Directly tests manual therapy adjunct to exercise.

RCT comparing sodium hyaluronate injection, steroid injection, physical therapy modalities, and control in adhesive capsulitis. The physical therapy intervention is described only as 'modalities' (likely electrotherapy) with no mention of manual therapy or exercise. The review focuses on manual therapy and exercise interventions.
Laboratory EMG study measuring muscle activation during therapeutic exercises in healthy and shoulder pain subjects. Not a treatment trial assessing efficacy for adhesive capsulitis.
Comparative study of three approaches for chronic shoulder pain. Population not confirmed as adhesive capsulitis, and abstract does not indicate randomised design.

RCT (20 patients) randomly divided into local corticosteroid injection versus physical therapy measures for adhesive capsulitis. Population is explicitly adhesive capsulitis and design is RCT. Specific PT content is not detailed, but eligible for full-text review given conservative screening.
Methodological chapter on interpreting results and drawing conclusions. Not a primary study.
Retrospective study of 130 patients with painful stiff shoulder assessing response to treatment. Not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial.
Randomised controlled study comparing Mulligan's versus Maitland's mobilization techniques in adhesive capsulitis of the shoulder. Compares two manual therapy approaches in the target population.
Methodological chapter on presenting results and Summary of findings tables. Not a primary study.
Observational epidemiological study of consultation prevalence for shoulder pain diagnoses. Not a treatment trial.
RCT comparing iodex iontophoresis, iodex phonophoresis, and placebo for shoulder periarthritis. Interventions are electrotherapy drug-delivery methods, not manual therapy or exercise.

Prospective randomised trial of 62 patients with painful stiff shoulder (not explicitly adhesive capsulitis/frozen shoulder) comparing local steroid, physiotherapy, or both. Population not confirmed as adhesive capsulitis; physiotherapy content unspecified.

Double-blind RCT (70 subjects) with frozen shoulder allocated to electroacupuncture plus exercise, interferential electrotherapy plus exercise, or no-treatment control. Intervention groups include shoulder exercise, and the control is no treatment, providing a relevant comparison for exercise-based management.

RCT (122 subjects) randomly allocated to ibuprofen alone versus ibuprofen plus combined physical therapy for adhesive capsulitis. Eligible population with RCT design comparing physical therapy adjunct versus medication alone.

Randomised controlled trial (22 patients) with adhesive capsulitis comparing exercises and ultrasound versus exercises, ultrasound, and end-range mobilization. Compares manual therapy added to a base exercise program.

Randomized clinical trial (20 subjects) with adhesive capsulitis randomly assigned to anterior versus posterior glide mobilization (plus ultrasound and ergometer exercise). Compares two manual therapy techniques.

RCT (80 patients) with adhesive capsulitis randomized to intra-articular triamcinolone plus physiotherapy, triamcinolone alone, placebo plus physiotherapy, or placebo alone. All given a home exercise programme. Includes relevant comparisons of physiotherapy/exercise versus control.

Prospective randomised study (72 patients) with adhesive capsulitis comparing manipulation under anaesthesia, peri-articular injection, and physiotherapy. Includes relevant physiotherapy comparison in the target population.
Systematic review of conservative and surgical interventions for frozen shoulder. Not a primary study.
Methodological chapter on analysing data and undertaking meta-analyses. Not a primary study.

Prospective investigation of 120 patients analysing outcomes by frequency of mobilization sessions and self-exercise compliance. The abstract describes an observational analysis of treatment factors rather than a randomised comparison of mobilization versus self-exercises.

Prospective clinical trial with systematic allocation (quasi-randomised) comparing chiropractic manipulation plus exercise versus chiropractic mobilization plus exercise in stage 2-3 frozen shoulder. Compares manual therapy interventions with exercise.
RCT (100 subjects) with adhesive capsulitis randomly assigned to high-grade mobilization techniques versus low-grade mobilization techniques. Compares two manual therapy approaches.

Single-blinded experimental pilot study randomising 14 subjects with adhesive capsulitis to home-care versus home-care plus passive mobilisation after corticosteroid injection. Small pilot RCT evaluating adjunct manual therapy.
